lines.en: : Ughhhhh. These shoes are killing me. I should have listened to my mom and gotten my own instead of borrowing hers.
: Just take them off. Ain’t nobody gonna give a shit. People know better than to mess with brides by now.
: No. I’ll just continue to suffer in silence until my feet need to be amputated and I’m never able to kick a soccer ball again. Or anything for that matter because...you know. No feet.
: I think kicking stuff will be the least of your worries if things come to that, Karin.
: True. But, on the bright side, I wouldn’t tower over everyone anymore. And that sounds like it might be kind of nice.
: For real. All these tiny bitches got me feeling like Shaq up in here. Which would probably make you Yao Ming since you’re even taller than I am.
: And better at shooting free throws.
: Now, how the hell do you know that? Ain’t neither of those two played since you were learning how to write yo’ damn name.

: My dad’s big on American sports. It’s probably how I wound up getting into them in the first place. The two of us used to watch basketball together and I just remember being impressed by their...size.
: Fuck was that pause for? Picked a damn weird time to hesitate, girl. Get your mind out of the gutter.
: I don’t know why I hesitated! It just happened! I was probably just...distracted by thinking about how big they are!
: You’d be diggin’ yourself into a hell of a hole right now if I was legally allowed to make sex jokes to you.
: Shh! Don’t say the “S” word in public! It’s inappropriate and you’re going to rile Kirin up.

: Oh, please. That girl’s been riled up since she hit puberty and she ain’t comin’ down any time soon. Especially not with a sister who was conceived by what I can only imagine as a fuckin’...cloud and a smile.
: It was only a minute ago that I was telling a story about my dad. Don’t go replacing him with a cloud just because Kirin is...maturing at a frightening pace.
: At least you’re willing to acknowledge it. Was starting to worry you were so deep in your own world that you didn’t even realize what kind of shit she’s into.
: It would be hard not to after watching her make a complete fool of herself during that God-awful swimsuit competition.
: Poor Sensei, being forced to quietly sit through all of that and choose a winner. He must have felt so uncomfortable.
: Yeah. Poor him. It must have been Hell.
: That’s enough of that, though. I have news.
: You do? Is it about the Ami thing?
: It is. But I did not say it was good news.
: Man, then what in Shaq’s sack is that smile for? Fuckin’ wholesome ass face got me thinkin’ you cracked the case wide open.
: Quite the opposite actually. I’m just smiling because life is great and I’m happy to have been invited to the Halloween party again.
: Spill it, then. What’s the “news?”
: The news is mostly just that...there isn’t much news at all. And what I mean by that is my dad can’t find any “hard” evidence connecting Ami to the girl from his class.
: We went through all of his old yearbooks together and couldn’t find a single picture of her.
: But, according to him, she was one of those “Only shows up to class when she wants to” types. So I guess it makes sense that she wouldn’t have gone to class picture day.
: So, what you’re saying is we ain’t got shit.
: Yes!
: Lord have mercy.
: But!
: But?
: He thinks he remembers her name. Or...her given name at least.
: Correct me if I’m wrong here, but shouldn’t it be the other way around? Cause unless your dad and Ami-Mommy were studying over in the west, that shit’s kinda weird.
: I believe the word he used to describe her was ”eccentric” and that she wouldn’t respond to her family name.
: Well, that might be something to go off of. Makes looking her up a little harder since the registry ain’t gonna tell us shit without a family name, but it’s better than nothing I guess.
: I agree. I’m really sorry I couldn’t help any more, though. But I know you and Miss Watabe will do everything you can to help Ami.
: The name, Karin. What is it?
: Oh, sorry. It’s S-
: Hi! What are you guys talking about?
: Salvador Dali!
: Sal...vation...Dolly?
: Yup! That’s him!
: You can finish telling me about Salvador Dali later, Karin. We don’t want to bore Ami with all of our...famous painter facts.
: Don’t let me stop you. I have a few minutes to kill while Sensei is outside. So, what’s all this about famous painters? What kind of facts do you know?
: Van Gogh chopped his ear off! And...uhh...Picasso was a cube!
: You weren’t talking about painting at all, were you?
: No, Ami. We weren’t talking about painting. But we were talking about something private and I think we’d both appreciate it a lot if you stopped prying and just left it at that.
: Sorry, Miss Imai. I’ve heard I can be kind of suffocating at times. But I promise I wasn’t trying to stop you from breathing or anything like that. I was just curious.
: Well...thank you for...not wanting to suffocate me. I’ll remember that when it comes time to grade your next quiz.
: Oh, you don’t have to go out of your way for me. I know I can be a real idiot when it comes to schoolwork sometimes, but I can still hold my own when I have to.
: You’re not an idiot, Ami. Senpai’s probably just been a little too easy on you for your whole ass life and that’s just now catching up to you. But it ain’t nothing a little overtime won’t fix.
: Are you saying that Sensei has done a bad job raising me?
: What?
: Are you saying Sensei has failed me? That you’d have raised me differently? That he’s not loving me the way he’s supposed to?
: Uhh...let’s back up for a second. I think there might be some sort of misunderstanding here.
: I don’t know anything about raising anyone. I just know that there are academic levels girls your age are expected to reach and...you are slightly beneath them. That’s all I’m saying.
: Do you want children one day, Miss Imai?
: This...is taking a weird turn.
: Do you think you’d be a good mom?
: I...haven’t put much thought into that just yet...
: I see.
: Ami...sorry if this is blunt, but...are you doing okay? Cause you seem kinda...not okay right now. And by “kinda” I mean you seem really not okay.
: I want kids some day.
: A lot of them.
: I’m good at taking care of people.
: In fact, I’ve been taking care of Sensei since long before you were even employed here.
: Ami, hold up. This-
: Which is why I really hope you were being honest when you said there was a misunderstanding just now.
: Because, if there is anything I don’t like, it’s when people talk badly about my uncle. You shouldn’t do that, Miss Imai.
: Girl, you ain’t got the faintest idea how I feel about your damn uncle.
: What is that supposed to mean?
: It’s supposed to mean that I ain’t tryin’ to talk down on the guy. I just want you to learn more shit. Ain’t no reason to get all Hannibal Lecter on me.
: You’d understand if you were in my shoes. But you don’t have anything to protect, so you don’t get it at all.
: Ami-
: It’s rude to talk about people while they’re not around.
: But it’s nothing compared to thinking you need to fix them.
: Ami, Miss Imai is just trying to-
: She should stop.
: You both should.
: Why is this human button a rotating plastic lever? I am incapable of pushing in that which refuses to be pushed!
: It’s called an analog stick, Kaori. You use it to move your character around — which I highly recommend you start doing before you die.
: I was not properly made aware of the potential consequences this game could have on my life! Human technology has become far too advanced in far too short of a time!
: This game is from, like...2002. Technology’s gotten a lot better since then.
: I...hope it has advanced to...a point where it can no longer end our lives!
: Hate to break it to you, but I think we’re actually ten times closer to what I can only imagine will be the inevitable truth of that fear being realized.
: It fell asleep on me.
: Its name is Nao-chan and the sleep function engages when too many spoons have been left behind. You can re-engage her “awake” function by gently blowing mouth-wind into her hearing-holes.
: Yeah, I’m not going to do that.
: I respect your cotton decision, candy girl. Now, please lessen the movement of your vocal vibrations before Nao-chan wakes up in a new, undiscovered way.
: Yeah, Niki. Keep your voice down. We’re trying to be gamers over here.
: You sound like a forty year old woman pretending to be young again by engaging in young people activities.
: You mean like how you’re almost thirty and your fanbase still thinks you’re like...what was it? Twelve?
: Listen here, you little shit. I-
: Shh!
: Oh, right. Childspawn.
: Continued usage of the stretchy voice tubes in your head-holder will separate her vision balls from the thin layers of flesh currently obscuring them.
: Yeah, I’m aware. I just haven’t had to deal with this since Noriko was a toddler.
: What is a “Noriko” and why does it no longer “toddle?”
: Noriko’s her sister. Think Niki but...less hot.
: By how many degrees?
: At least seven.
: Seven degrees below normal human body temperature could be fatal. I now understand why the Noriko no longer toddles.
: Having fun over there, Niki?
: Not particularly.
: I guess I don’t hate it, though.
: This one’s fine because she doesn’t make noise even when she’s awake. Plus, she’s a lot cuter without that stupid hat on.
: Nao-chan chose that cranial covering herself! It is your soft skull-protector that is stupid! Hers is beautiful and reinforces the idea of criminal justice!
: Sure...whatever...sorry.
: Woah. You’re not even going to clap back? You getting baby fever over there or something?
: Me? Absolutely not. Didn't I just mention not wanting kids when we were upstairs?
: Besides, I’d be a terrible mother.
: Why do you say that, fluffy pink sugar-ball?
: Well, for one, I’d have zero time to spend with a daughter.
: Kinda weird that you’ve already chosen the sex of the baby you’re not going to have.
: Of course I’d have a girl. Boys suck and I’d just return a son if I ever had one.
: To...where?
: I think a bigger problem than just the time thing, though, is that...I’m just not really sure if I’d be able to love it.
: And now she’s an it?

: I’m already spread thin wasting all of my worries on my stupid boyfriend. And the shitty truth is that I have a finite amount of love to give, so it’s not like I’m going to make him suffer instead of some kid.
: Especially one I barely even know.
: I read inside the guts of a dead tree that mothermoms imprint on their children the way birds imprint on other birds. So I believe you would know the childspawn. Or at least feel like you do.
: Maybe that’s true. Maybe there is something special about the bond between a mother and her child...I’ve always loved my parents, after all. And I never needed a reason to do that...
: But what if my kid doesn’t like me? Or what if I don’t like them? What if they take after their stupid fucking dad and just bitch and moan all day long about literally nothing?
: And here I thought you loved those qualities in Sensei.
: Obviously not, Otoha. But just because I love him doesn’t mean I love everything about him. He annoys me more than everyone else in the world combined.
: Hey, cool. I was worried I might be in first place after Christmas.
: Keep bringing it up and you might take the lead. But, for now...
: It’s only him.
: And he’ll never want kids. He wouldn’t be able to handle them.
: He’s too...fragile.
: He seems to handle Ami just fine and she’s basically his kid.
: Those two handle each other. And after what they’ve gone through, I don’t think it’s really fair to compare their bond to...well, anything.

: Besides, Ami will probably be in college by the time Akira’s ready to settle down. So we won’t even have her to look after the kid when we both inevitably want nothing to do with it. Or her. Or whatever.
: Yeah, I don’t think finding a babysitter with your income would be a particularly difficult thing to do. Just saying.
: Yeah. Maybe not.
: I guess having one on accident wouldn’t be the end of the world, though.
: I’d just want to skip the first, like...five years of its life. Or maybe six.
: I’ll tag in once it hits seven.
: Mother of the year over here. Pretty soon, you’ll be-
: Ahah! I have figured out the secrets of the plastic joyful twig!
: I’m the video game girl! I’m the one who wins!
: Kaori, shh. Childspawn.
: If you yell, she’ll...
Two hours later...
